stages.title: Economic systems
stages.sub: How different economies decide who gets the scarce goods and services.

steps.q: A baker has 10 loaves and 30 buyers. If the price rises until only 10 still want one, who gets the bread?
steps.right: Whoever is willing and able to pay the price
steps.wrong: The government, by handing out ration cards
steps.hint: Nobody has stepped in to allocate the bread. What is doing the sorting instead?

steps.q: Instead, a ministry decides in advance how many loaves each bakery makes and who receives them. Who now decides who gets bread?
steps.right: A central authority deciding in advance
steps.wrong: Whoever gets to the bakery first each morning
steps.hint: There is no price doing the sorting here. Who is making the decision instead?
steps.pre: So a central body deciding what and how much to produce is

steps.q: Bakers, farmers and shoppers set their own prices, and no ministry directs them. Who decides what gets made?
steps.wrong: A government department, through a plan
steps.hint: Think about what you just called the system where prices alone sort out who gets the bread.

steps.wrong: Individuals, through prices they set themselves

steps.q: Shops set most prices freely, but the government runs hospitals, schools and roads. Is one system used, or both together?
steps.right: Both systems are being used together
steps.wrong: Only one of the systems is being used
